title: 15 US universities with the highest acceptance rates for international students
summary: These 15 US universities admitted over 90% of international applicants. See each rate, the cost to prove for an I-20 and visa rules. Compare your options.
body_markdown:
The US universities with the highest acceptance rates admit nine or more of every ten international students who apply. On the latest U.S. News figures (fall 2023 admissions, published in the 2025 Best Colleges edition), the University of Mississippi accepted 98.96% of international applicants. Missouri Southern State University (98.45%), UNC Pembroke (98.16%) and Kansas State University (98.01%) were close behind.


That is remarkable when the average across the 360 ranked universities that reported this number was 39.1%. But for a student in Lagos, Accra or Nairobi, the offer letter is rarely the hard part. The harder tests come after it: proving you can pay for a full year before the school issues your I-20, and getting the visa.


Below are all 15 schools on that list, what six of them say a year costs an international undergraduate, the steps from offer to visa, the 2026 visa restriction every Nigerian applicant needs to know about, and how to pay a US school from abroad without losing money in fees.


## The 15 US universities with the highest acceptance rates for international students


U.S. News ranked these universities by the share of international first-year applicants they admitted for fall 2023, using data the schools reported. Only ranked universities that received at least 500 international applications were counted, so very small colleges are not on the list.

Source: U.S. News & World Report list of universities with the highest acceptance rates for international students, fall 2023 data, as[republished by WTOP](https://wtop.com/news/2024/10/13-universities-with-the-highest-international-student-acceptance-rates) on 24 October 2024. These are the most recent international-only figures we could verify on 27 November 2026, and rates move every year, so check each school's latest number before you apply.


Most of these schools are large public universities in the Midwest and South. Nine of the 15 are in the U.S. News National Universities category, so a high acceptance rate here does not mean a small or unknown college.


A high rate is still not guaranteed entry. Each school sets its own minimum grades and English test scores, and the rate only shows how many of the students who applied were admitted.


## What a year costs at six of these universities


Before a US university issues your I-20, the form you need for an F-1 student visa, it asks you to prove you can pay for your first year. The University of Kansas, for example, says you must submit[proof of financial support](https://world.ku.edu/costs) before it can issue an I-20.


So the number that decides whether you can go is not the acceptance rate. It is the yearly cost the school expects to see covered in your bank statements or sponsor letters.


University International acceptance rate, fall 2023 (%) Estimated cost for one year (USD) What the school's figure covers


[South Dakota State University](https://www.sdstate.edu/admissions/estimated-costs-international-students) 93.60 29,795 Annual estimate: tuition and fees ($16,284) and living expenses ($9,814); personal spending of $500 to $2,000 a year is extra


[Kent State University](https://www.kent.edu/admissions/international-tuition-and-fees) 90.56 42,593 2026-2027 estimate used for I-20s: tuition and fees ($24,298), living ($14,360), insurance and books ($3,935)


[Kansas State University](https://www.k-state.edu/admissions/undergrad/manhattan/apply/international/i20costs.html) 98.01 48,769 Fall and spring I-20 amount: tuition and fees ($31,845), living ($15,872), books ($1,052)


[University of Mississippi](https://olemiss.edu/admissions/undergraduate-admissions/tuition-and-fees/index.php) 98.96 50,810 Out-of-state cost of attendance for two semesters; no separate international figure on this page


[Northern Arizona University](https://in.nau.edu/center-international-education/tuition-fees/) 95.16 51,940 2026-2027 I-20 estimate: tuition and fees ($32,757), housing and meals ($15,407), books and health insurance ($3,776)


[University of Kansas](https://world.ku.edu/costs) 95.28 52,278 Tuition and fees ($33,854) plus living costs, books and health insurance ($18,424)


Checked 27 November 2026 on each university's international admissions or cost page. Kent State and Northern Arizona label their figures 2026-2027; the other four pages do not state an academic year.


Here is what most "easy admission" lists leave out. On these numbers, getting into Kansas State is close to a formality, but its I-20 amount asks you or a sponsor to show $48,769 for the year. South Dakota State admits a slightly smaller share of international applicants, yet its own estimate is about $19,000 lower.


So when you compare high-acceptance schools, sort them by the yearly cost you can prove, not by the acceptance rate. A 93% chance at a school you can fund beats a 98% chance at one you can't. If the figure is out of reach, look at[study abroad funding](https://grey.co/blog/5-ways-to-get-funding-to-study-abroad-in-2024) before you rule a school out.


## From offer letter to visa: the steps in order


1. **Apply to each school.** Check the international application fee, deadline and English test requirement on its admissions page.
2. **Accept your offer and send financial documents.** The school checks that your bank statements or sponsor letters cover its yearly estimate, then issues your I-20.
3. **Pay the SEVIS I-901 fee.** It is[$350 for F-1 students](https://ice.gov/sevis/i901) , according to US Immigration and Customs Enforcement.
4. **Complete the DS-160 and book your visa interview.** Check the current application fee on the[State Department fees page](https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/us-visas/visa-information-resources/fees/fees-visa-services.html) .
5. **Pay your deposit or first-semester tuition.** Ask which payments are refundable if your visa is refused, before you send anything.


Our[student visa guide](https://grey.co/blog/applying-for-a-us-student-visa-a-detailed-guide-for-2024) covers the DS-160 and the interview in more detail.


## Nigerian applicants: check the 2026 visa restriction first


Since 1 January 2026, Presidential Proclamation 10998 has partially suspended new US visas for Nigerian nationals, including F and M student visas and J exchange visas. The University of North Texas international office, in an[update current as of 16 November 2026](https://international.unt.edu/international-students/immigration-updates.html) , still lists Nigeria among the partially restricted countries, alongside Benin, Côte d'Ivoire, Senegal, Tanzania, Zambia and Zimbabwe.


The US Mission in Nigeria said in February 2026 that Nigerians who already hold[valid F-1 or J-1 visas](https://nairametrics.com/2026/02/24/visa-restrictions-us-says-nigerian-students-with-valid-f1-j1-visas-unaffected/) are not affected. If you don't yet have a student visa, an offer letter will not get you one while the restriction stands, apart from limited exceptions, so hold off on non-refundable deposits until you have checked the latest position with the school and the US Embassy.


Ghana, Kenya, Egypt and Pakistan were not on the full or partial lists on that page when we checked on 27 November 2026. The rules changed in June 2025 and again in December 2025, so check again before you pay.


## How to pay a US university from Nigeria, Ghana or Kenya


Once you have an I-20 and a visa route, the next job is moving tuition from naira, cedis or shillings into dollars at the school. If your university accepts a domestic US bank transfer (ACH), you can[send USD](https://grey.co/send-usd) to it from a Grey USD balance.


Grey's published ACH terms, checked 27 November 2026: each transfer can be $10 to $5,000, it usually clears in 1 to 2 business days, and the fee is 0.5% per transfer with a minimum of $2 and a maximum of $10. Converting your local currency to USD in Grey costs 1%, capped at $6.

Checked 27 November 2026. The total excludes the exchange rate, which the app shows before you confirm; if you convert in several batches, each conversion is capped at $6. Check today's[USD to NGN rate](https://grey.co/convert/en/usd-to-ngn) ,[USD to GHS](https://grey.co/convert/en/usd-to-ghs) or[USD to KES](https://grey.co/convert/en/usd-to-kes) before you budget.


Three habits stop a payment going missing. Put your student ID in the reference, send at least three business days before the deadline, and email the student accounts office your receipt, because Grey notes that ACH payments are not traceable.


Some universities take international payments only through their own payment portal or by international wire, so check your school's payment page first. For application fees and other online charges, a Grey[virtual card](https://grey.co/cards) can pay online card charges and costs $5 to create.


Parents in Nigeria can follow our[school fees guide](https://grey.co/blog/pay-us-school-fees-from-nigeria) to add the university as a recipient, and families in Egypt have an[Egypt-specific guide](https://grey.co/blog/how-egyptian-students-pay-school-fees-abroad-with-grey) . Grey is a financial technology company, not a bank.


## Frequently asked questions


### Which US university has the highest acceptance rate for international students?


On the latest U.S. News list we could verify (fall 2023 data), the University of Mississippi (Ole Miss) had the highest rate, admitting 98.96% of international applicants. Missouri Southern State University (98.45%) and the University of North Carolina at Pembroke (98.16%) came next.


### Is a high acceptance rate a bad sign?


Not by itself. Nine of the 15 schools on this list sit in the U.S. News National Universities category. A high rate tells you how selective the admissions office is, not how good your course will be, so compare programmes, costs and graduate outcomes too.


### How much money do I need to show for an I-20?


You need to show the school's estimated cost for one year. On the university pages we checked on 27 November 2026, that ranged from $29,795 at South Dakota State University to $52,278 at the University of Kansas.


### Can Nigerians get a US student visa in 2026?


Nigerians who already hold a valid F-1 or J-1 visa are not affected by Presidential Proclamation 10998, according to the US Mission in Nigeria. New F, M and J visas for Nigerian nationals have been partially suspended since 1 January 2026, so check the current position with the US Embassy before you pay any deposit.


## Where to start


A 98% acceptance rate feels like the finish line, but it is only the first gate. The real filters are the yearly cost you can prove and the visa you can get.


Shortlist two or three schools you can fund, confirm your visa route, then plan how the money will move. When you arrive, our guide to[banking options](https://grey.co/blog/best-bank-alternatives-for-international-students-in-the-us-and-uk) covers everyday money in the US, and a[Grey account](https://grey.co/) lets you pay tuition in dollars when the bill comes.
